ACCOUNT SUMMARY
- Prospect: HelixBank (enterprise security posture; internal platform team evaluating LLM inference for contact center + internal knowledge workflows).
- Target deployment: Redwood Private in HelixBank VPC (no public ingress from Helix to vendor; allowlist + private connectivity only).
- Workloads discussed:
  - Tier 1/2 agent assist (chat w/ citations), low latency target, needs consistent throughput.
  - Summarization of call notes + case history; batch-friendly.
  - Embeddings for internal policy/KB search (moderate volume, strict access boundaries).

KEY REQUIREMENTS (SECURITY / COMPLIANCE)
- RBAC granularity is a gating item. They explicitly called out: "We cannot onboard a system where Admin means everything. We need least privilege + separation-of-duties." 
- Default roles must cover: Org Admin, Security Admin, Billing Admin, Developer, Read-only, and a Support/Impersonation role that is tightly controlled.
- Custom roles: strongly preferred (at minimum: ability to create a role that can export audit logs but cannot view billing / cannot change SSO).
- SSO/SAML required. Needs mapping from IdP groups -> roles (SCIM nice-to-have, but they will accept manual mapping initially if documented).
- Audit logs:
  - Must include authz decision metadata for privileged actions (allow/deny, reason code, actor identity, role IDs, policy version).
  - Export to SIEM; they asked for stable event schema and backward compatibility story.
  - Retention controls: they want 365d in their SIEM; Redwood retention can be shorter but export must be reliable.
- Break-glass / support:
  - No standing access by support.
  - If support impersonation exists, must be time-bounded, approval-based, and produce explicit audit events + alerting.

PERFORMANCE / PRODUCT NOTES
- Latency targets mentioned on call:
  - Agent assist: p95 < 1.5s for first token in-region (they care about perceived responsiveness).
  - Streaming required.
- They were open to Dedicated for early POC, but for production they want Private.
- Residency: US regions only.

TIMELINE / ACTIVITY LOG (RECENT)
- 2025-01-23 (Discovery): Platform Eng intro; aligned on Private deployment + security review prerequisites.
- 2025-02-11 (Security review call): Fireflies ff_9b7c2a1d_security-review_redwood_rbac. Focused heavily on RBAC, custom roles, and audit evidence. Action items: share RBAC v2 overview + describe default roles; confirm audit log fields + export path.
- 2025-02-19 (Email follow-up): Sent preliminary answers to enterprise questionnaire; Helix replied with additional RBAC-specific questions (Gmail: thread_rbac_v2_enterprise_questionnaire_2025_02). They requested explicit role matrix + examples of least-privilege for API key management + SSO settings.
- 2025-03-06 (GRC review): Helix asked for SOC 2 alignment and evidence artifacts. Olga looped in for control mapping requests (Gmail: thread_soc2_control_mapping_rbac_v2_2025_03). They want sample audit events that include authz decision context.
- 2025-03-18 (Internal): SE flagged procurement is blocked until RBAC v2 is GA + documented for Private (policy distribution / versioning story).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS
- Custom roles: Helix wants commitment/timeline. They will not accept "defaults only" long-term.
- Support model for Private: they asked if Redwood can do zero-access support (preferred). If not, require strict break-glass with approvals from Helix Security.
- Policy distribution: asked how RBAC policies are updated in Private (esp. change control). They want signed artifacts + version pinning.

NEXT STEPS (OWNER/SE)
- Send: RBAC v2 overview + default role definitions + migration/GA timeline (include what is available in shadow mode vs enforced).
- Provide: example audit log events showing authz decision fields, plus SIEM export mapping.
- Schedule: follow-up with Helix Security + Redwood Security Eng (Marcus/Kevin) once GA date is firm.
- Confirm: Private policy bundle update mechanism + how version skew is handled during upgrades.

INTERNAL NOTES (SHORTHAND)
- Buyer: Security + Platform; Procurement will follow once security checklist is green.
- Tone: skeptical until we can demonstrate least privilege + auditability. Very specific on SoD (billing vs security).
- Quote (security lead): "If we can’t prove who was allowed to do what, and why, it won’t pass internal audit."
